To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

discourse segmentation is a function of the interaction of the following factors: (1) the discourse structure of the sentence, (2) the discourse structure at the sentence boundary, (3) the discourse structure following the sentence boundary, and (4) the discourse function of the sentence boundary.

the semantic interpretation of a sentence is determined by the following factors: (i) the semantic and syntactic properties of the words in the sentence, and the syntactic and semantic properties of the phrases and clauses of which the sentence is composed; (ii) the semantic properties of the discourse segment in which the sentence is embedded; and (iii) the semantic properties and discourse function of the sentence relative to the discourse segment in question.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: 1) Discourse Segmentation: The problem of how to identify the boundaries between the discourse segments that make up the text.
developing a formal theory of discourse understanding.
the following three issues: (1) The segmentation and organization of discourse; (2) The interpretation of discourse segments; and (3) The interaction of discourse and sentence level semantics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

discourse understanding research is a complex, multi-disciplinary field which involves the development of formal models of discourse segmentation, sequential organization and interpretation, and the development of sentential linguistic and pragmatic theories to provide the discourse model with structural, semantic, and pragmatic information.

discourse understanding is the study of the formal mechanisms which allow us to assign semantic interpretations to the surface structure of language and to integrate these interpretations into a coherent, contextually appropriate, and contextually constrained whole.
discourse understanding is the study of the principles and mechanisms by which a language user can assign proper semantic interpretations to surface linguistic forms in context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it has been concerned with developing a formal model of the discourse structure and interpretation of texts, and with developing a computational implementation of that model.
we are developing a formal theory of the semantics of discourse, which we call Discourse Representation Theory (DRT).
it has been concerned primarily with developing the formal mechanisms for discourse segmentation, sequential organization and interpretation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the discourse structure of a text is a complex, hierarchical, and dynamic phenomenon which is best modelled by a formal grammar of discourse which is both compositional and context-sensitive.

the discourse understanding problem can be decomposed into a number of more tractable sub-problems, which can be addressed by combining the techniques of discourse theory with those of formal semantics, pragmatics and syntax.

discourse structure is not a simple matter of sentence concatenation, nor a matter of simple linear ordering, and that it is not a matter of the application of a simple, linearly ordered set of rules to the surface structure of the discourse.
